description: Hi! We are team shipX participating from theCalicutevent. We are focusing on creative storytelling and digital exhibits exploring humanity's discarded technology across the Moon and Mars. Looking forward to an amazing and creative hackathon journey!
summary: shipX tells the story of humanity’s left-behind hardware on the Moon and Mars through a digital “Museum of Left-Behind Machines” made for school-age space fans. Visitors explore a timeline of abandoned equipment, from Apollo-era landers and the Lunar Roving Vehicle to the silent Spirit rover, and read each machine’s story in the machine’s own voice: what it was built to do, what it discovered, and why it was left behind. Short quiz cards and “what we learned” facts connect each machine to the science it made possible. Using NASA mission information and public sources, the project shows that these machines are not junk but the first chapters of exploration that future missions build on. Abandoned, but not forgotten.
details:
What it does: An interactive story-exhibit where each abandoned NASA machine “narrates” its own mission, built for students aged 10 to 16.
Impact: Makes space history and engineering relatable, and shows how past missions enable future ones like Artemis.
Tools: HTML/CSS/JavaScript for the exhibit, Google Slides for the demo, NASA mission pages and the NASA Image and Video Library for facts
Creativity: Machines are given a first-person “voice”, turning data into storytelling.
Team consideration: Accuracy (all facts checked against NASA pages), age-appropriate language, and clear credit for all sources.
SI use: AI tools were used for brainstorming and for drafting and editing text. All facts were reviewed by the team against NASA sources.
